title: Edge proxy + batching integration exploration - Hightide Analytics
summary: Discovery call to understand Hightide's integration needs for Redwood (hosted vs dedicated vs private), gateway/proxy patterns, SDK usage (LangChain/LlamaIndex), rate limits and observability hooks. Discussed batching, KV/prefix cache, SSO/KMS requirements. Agreed to run a short benchmark and share security pack.
action_items: Alex Rivera - Share Redwood security whitepaper & SOC2 cert - due 2026-02-13
Priya Shah - Create initial benchmark plan and sample request patterns - due 2026-02-16
Tariq Khan - Provide example request/traffic profile and spike windows - due 2026-02-14
next_steps: Redwood to send security docs and pricing tiers
Customer to review benchmark plan and provide traffic samples
Schedule technical deep dive next week to look at private deployment checklist
transcript:
00:00:03 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, account exec for Hightide, quick roll call?
00:00:10 Morgan: Morning, Morgan here, product, excited to dig in
00:00:13 Tariq: Tariq, backend eng, we're mainly focused on reliability and cost
00:00:16 Samir: Samir, CTO, I'll be peeking in for a bit
00:00:21 Priya: Priya Shah, solutions eng at Redwood - I'll cover the technical side and the SDK patterns
00:01:05 Alex: Agenda - understand your stack, what you're trying to replace or improve, multi-tenant rate limiting, and integration patterns. We'll also cover hosted vs dedicated vs private. Feel free to interrupt.
00:02:02 Morgan: Quick background - we run realtime analytics for ads, low latency requirements for inference, we use a mixture of precomputed features and online LLMs for summarization and intent. Currently hitting token cost and occasional latency spikes during nightly batches. We're evaluating Redwood for inference serving and also to standardize on one gateway.
00:02:49 Alex: Got it. Are you thinking hosted first or on-prem/dedicated from day one?
00:03:04 Morgan: Prefer hosted to start, but must have private option within 6 months for data residency, and dedicated reserved capacity looks attractive if latency variance persists.
00:03:28 Priya: Makes sense. In our experience teams often start hosted and then commit to dedicated for predictable p95. We support pinning model versions and automatic fallbacks if a model variant is down.
00:04:10 Tariq: Two technical bits: we have an edge proxy in front of our services (Envoy-based) and we'd like to avoid a heavy sidecar per instance. Can Redwood act as a gateway/proxy that our edge can forward to, or do you prefer sidecar?
00:04:42 Priya: Both patterns are common. Gateway pattern works well if you want centralized routing and quotas; sidecar gives local caching benefits (KV cache) and reduces hop latency for hot prefixes. Gateway + prefix caching is supported — we have prefix/KV cache at the gateway layer but if you need sub-ms local cache, sidecar helps.
00:05:17 Morgan: When you say prefix cache, is that the same as KV cache I keep reading about?
00:05:22 Priya: Right, prefix/KV cache similar concept - caching KV pairs of the autoregressive context to avoid recomputing long prefixes. It's effective for assistant-like workloads or repeated prompts. It's called prefix cache in some docs, KV in others.
00:06:01 Tariq: What about SDKs — we use LangChain and a custom LlamaIndex ingestion pipeline. How's support?
00:06:22 Priya: We have SDK samples for Node/Python and explicit integrations/examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex; the SDK supports direct streaming, function calling, and structured outputs. We also have a gateway pattern example that shows a middleware translating LangChain calls to Redwood requests to enable batching.
00:06:55 Jordan: (chiming in) One pattern we've seen: LangChain agents call a local gateway which does request coalescing and continuous batching to the Redwood hosted endpoint. That reduces per-token costs because of batched decode efficiency while preserving low latency for singletons via time-sliced flush policies.
00:07:34 Morgan: Interesting. Can you show a sample of that pattern or share a code snippet?
00:07:43 Priya: We'll include a repo link — quick example we can share: middleware that buffers requests for up to X ms or N requests before flush. Works with LangChain's async LLM wrapper. We'll add that to the action items.
00:08:08 Samir: On quotas — we need per-customer rate limits, and also per-route token quotas. Can Redwood enforce multi-dimension quotas?
00:08:25 Priya: Yes, our platform supports token-based quotas by API key and route-level policies; for Dedicated/Private you can also set router-level throttles and per-tenant rate limits. We do have burst windows and refill rates; plus we surface rejected requests in the console.
00:08:58 Morgan: Do you do graceful degradation e.g., fallback to smaller model or cached responses if quota exceeded?
00:09:12 Priya: Exactly. We support fallback policies: automatic fallback to cheaper compatible model variants, region fallback, or a cache-first policy. You can configure those in rollout configs.
00:10:01 Tariq: Observability — we need traces correlated to our existing tracing (we run Jaeger/Zipkin) and logs forwarded to our ELK. Any hooks?
00:10:19 Priya: We export per-request traces and have a tracing hook that emits trace IDs compatible with OpenTelemetry. Logs and token-level cost breakdowns can stream to your endpoint or to S3, we also push metrics to Prometheus exporters for Dedicated.
00:11:05 Morgan: Are latency percentiles per-route available?
00:11:09 Priya: Yes — p50/p95/p99, per-model and per-route. The console shows token breakdowns and latency buckets. We can provide a sample dashboard.
00:11:46 Morgan: Security: SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS for encryption, and audit logs - are these available for Hosted?
00:11:58 Alex: Hosted customers get SOC2 and encryption at rest; for bring-your-own-key KMS, that's available on Dedicated and Private. SSO/SAML is available for enterprise tiers. We'll attach the security pack.
00:12:19 Samir: We also need audit logs that show token-level operations for compliance.
00:12:26 Priya: Audit logs are available and we can configure retention and export. For strict requirements, Private deployment on-prem gives maximal control and HSM options.
00:13:10 Morgan: On the topic of batching — we're worried about latency vs cost. Our product needs interactive latency for UI queries and bulk nightly scoring. How do you recommend configuring batching and caching?
00:13:34 Jordan: Typically we recommend two routes: an interactive low-latency route with small or no batching and a batched bulk route for nightly jobs that allows larger batch windows. Combined with prefix caching for repeated prompts, unit cost drops significantly for bulk. Our Optimize feature can suggest batch sizes based on observed token distributions.
00:14:15 Tariq: Can the gateway do continuous batching across tenants while preserving per-tenant quotas? That is, coalesce requests for efficiency but bill and rate-limit per-tenant?
00:14:31 Priya: Yes — the router tags requests with tenant metadata and we keep logical accounting per-tenant even when coalescing them into a single GPU batch. Billing and quotas are computed before batching is aggregated.
00:15:05 Morgan: Great. About private deployments — lead time and support?
00:15:16 Alex: Private (VPC or on-prem) usually takes 6-12 weeks depending on infra, security reviews, and access. We have a checklist (ops, network, KMS, audit) and a professional services track to help.
00:15:40 Samir: Any customers migrated from hosted to private? Any gotchas?
00:15:46 Priya: Yes — common gotchas: network peering and egress rules, GPU driver versions, and differences in autoscaling policies. We provide an onboarding repo and runbooks to minimize friction.
00:16:25 Morgan: What SLAs do you offer for Dedicated?
00:16:29 Alex: Dedicated has an SLA for uptime and p95 latency tiers depending on committed capacity. We'll share the SLA doc.
00:17:02 Tariq: For our LlamaIndex pipeline, we do vector similarity + LLM re-rank. Do you support embeddings + reranking in the same flow?
00:17:21 Priya: Yes. Our API supports embeddings generation and reranking endpoints. We also have an example where embeddings are stored externally (your vector DB) and the rerank call hits Redwood to score top-K candidates, with batching at the rerank step.
00:18:04 Morgan: Are there any sandbox limits we should anticipate when trying hosted?
00:18:12 Alex: For initial POC we provide dev quota and some free credits. We'll outline sandbox limits in the onboarding doc.
00:19:05 Jordan: If you'd like, we can propose a mini-POC: 1) Redwood runs a 48-hour bench on your request profile to show p95 and cost per 1M tokens for interactive and bulk paths; 2) LangChain/LlamaIndex integration sample repo; 3) security pack.
00:19:32 Morgan: That sounds exactly like what we need. We'll need the benchmark to include spike windows and 99th percentile behavior.
00:19:41 Priya: We'll capture that — please send your traffic pattern.
00:20:20 Tariq: One practical question: how do you surface throttled requests in the API — do you return 429 and a Retry-After header?
00:20:29 Priya: Yes 429 + Retry-After, and the console shows rejected counts and per-key throttling events. For gateway-based rate limits we can also emit webhooks on throttle if you want immediate alerting.
00:21:10 Morgan: For observability, can we attach our correlation ids to the Redwood call so traces tie back?
00:21:15 Priya: Absolutely - you can pass X-Request-ID or OpenTelemetry headers; those will propagate through our traces and show in the console.
00:22:00 Jordan: Quick note on token accounting: when requests are batched, we still allocate tokens per original request for billing and quota calculation; cost savings come from GPU decoding efficiency, not by splitting billing.
00:22:37 Morgan: Any limits on max sequence length for certain models? We use long-context occasionally for session replay summaries.
00:22:46 Priya: Models vary — we document model-specific max tokens in the catalog. For long-context workloads we recommend select models and sometimes quantized variants. We can also support context-window-aware kernel selection for Dedicated.
00:23:19 Tariq: Are there any SDK rate limiters we should use client-side to avoid thundering herd?
00:23:27 Jordan: We provide client-side middleware examples for exponential backoff and jitter, and recommend local request coalescing at the gateway. Avoid atomic retry storms by using a central backoff policy.
00:24:02 Morgan: Regarding pricing — do you price hosted per-token and have reserved pricing for dedicated?
00:24:08 Alex: Yes hosted is per-token; Dedicated has reserved capacity and committed monthly fees, plus usage tiers. We'll include a pricing sheet but final numbers depend on committed throughput and model selection.
00:24:50 Morgan: Any known integrations with our vector DB vendor, Veloria?
00:24:57 Priya: We have connectors and docs for common vector DBs; Veloria specifics we can validate but we've seen workarounds pattern for that.
00:25:25 Tariq: For the benchmark plan, what metrics will you collect?
00:25:30 Priya: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput (rps), token cost per request, GPU occupancy, batching efficiency, error rates, and memory/kv cache hit rates. We'll deliver a spreadsheet and dashboards.
00:26:12 Morgan: Perfect. One more: for compliance we need data residency for EU clients. Can Redwood host regionally for hosted?
00:26:23 Alex: Yes we have regional endpoints and can keep data in EU regions; private deployment gives full control. We'll note your EU requirement in the follow-ups.
00:27:05 Samir: Who will be our primary Redwood contact for the technical POC?
00:27:10 Priya: That'll be me (Priya) and Jordan for the bench. Alex will coordinate commercial.
00:27:58 Morgan: Any rough timeline if we start POC next week?
00:28:05 Alex: Quick POC (bench + sample integration) usually 1-2 weeks, deeper private work a month plus. We'll draft a schedule.
00:29:20 Tariq: We will send a sample of our request distribution CSV and a small set of prompts for caching tests.
00:29:33 Morgan: We'll also loop in security and infra for the private checklist review.
00:30:01 Priya: Noted. We'll include the onboarding runbook and the private deployment checklist.
00:30:45 Jordan: Small gotcha note — if you run a gateway coalescer, make sure the upstream preserves per-request metadata (tenant id, request id) so we can do accounting.
00:31:12 Morgan: Good call.
00:31:45 Samir: Any outstanding concerns from our side?
00:31:50 Tariq: Just to be explicit — we need per-tenant quotas, a fallback path for when quotas hit, and detailed traceability for audits.
00:32:02 Priya: Confirmed. We'll ensure the benchmark and POC include fallback scenarios and traceability verification.
00:33:10 Morgan: Alright let's recap next steps.
00:33:15 Alex: Recap - Redwood: security docs, benchmark plan, sample LangChain middleware repo. Hightide: traffic profile CSV, spike windows, and internal stakeholders for security review. We'll schedule the tech deep dive next Tue.
00:34:00 Morgan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
00:34:05 Priya: Thanks, we'll send the pack by Friday.
00:34:12 Alex: End call.
00:54:00 [recording ends]
